name: iHeartMedia, Inc.

shortInterest.source: equibles.com (6.2M shares short, 4.0% of float, 10.3 days to cover, described as rising)

cash.source: secondary analysis of Q3 2026 10-Q (cash fell from $174.4M in June 2026)

debt.note: Not established from available sources, though iHeartMedia carries a large legacy debt load referenced qualitatively by multiple sources.

pe.note: negative earnings (GAAP net losses in FY2024, FY2025, and Q3 2026)

eps.note: Reported loss of $0.06/share, wider than the analyst estimate of a $0.02 loss, per RBR/Benzinga coverage; a separate secondary aggregator figure of -$0.54 for 'Q3' conflicts and is likely mislabeled/misdated (see conflicts).

price.note: No separately confirmed Nov 11, 2026 close was found; most recent dated figure is the post-earnings Nov 10, 2026 session (new 52-week low). Stock closed at $0.62 (CNBC snapshot showed $0.598-$0.6095 intraday, -66.2%) on volume of 38.88M shares; this is the day after the Nov 9 earnings release and may be the move the task's 'fell ~29% premarket' note is referencing (see conflicts).

catalysts.headline: Law firm 'SueWallSt' issued a shareholder-investigation notice regarding potential securities claims tied to the stock's collapse (solicitation-style release, not a regulatory action)
iHeartMedia fell ~29% premarket after its Q3 2026 report; no further detail (reported figures, consensus comparison) located beyond the aggregator mover headline this session.
iHeartMedia CEO warned major advertisers are delaying spending as economic uncertainty bites, cited as driver of continued share weakness the day after earnings

iHeartMedia Q3 2026 results: revenue $1.03B (+3.3% YoY, +1% ex-political); Adjusted EBITDA $170.5M, down 16.7% YoY and below the company's own $180-220M plan; GAAP EPS loss of $0.06 (vs -$0.02 est.); Multiplatform Group (broadcast) segment adjusted EBITDA fell 42.9%; Digital Audio Group revenue +13.8% but segment EBITDA -2.3%; podcast revenue +24.4% to $173.7M; free cash flow -$10.4M for the quarter; cash fell to $139.7M from $174.4M at June 2026; company cut full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $550M-$600M from the prior ~$800M target cited on prior calls, largely on weaker-than-expected political advertising, advertiser spending delays amid macro uncertainty, and a shift to programmatic audio buying
catalysts.impact: Shares fell sharply; reported after-hours decline of approximately 35-37%, with the stock later touching a new 52-week low intraday around -66% to $0.598-$0.6095 before settling near $0.62

conflicts: The magnitude of the post-earnings decline is reported very inconsistently: ~35-37% after-hours on Nov 9 per one summary, vs. an intraday move described as 'down 66%' to ~$0.60-$0.61 on Nov 10 per a CNBC/finwire snapshot (52-week-low date listed as 11/10/26). The task's stated figure of '~29% premarket' does not closely match either of these; it may reflect only the initial premarket print before the stock continued falling intraday and the next day.

Q3 2026 EPS reported as -$0.06 (RBR/Benzinga-sourced commentary) vs. a MarketBeat aggregator figure of -$0.54 against a -$0.28 estimate dated to a URL labeled 2026-08-10 (likely a different/mislabeled quarter) -- not reconciled.

Full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance: multiple prior-quarter previews said management had reaffirmed ~$800M full-year Adjusted EBITDA and $200M free cash flow targets through Q2 2026 calls; the Q3 2026 release is reported by one source as cutting that full-year target to $550M-$600M, while another secondary summary suggests only the quarter missed plan without explicitly confirming a formal full-year guidance cut. Treat the guidance-cut framing as sourced from secondary commentary, not a directly read primary release.

Market cap/shares outstanding/short interest figures above are from an Aug 20, 2026 snapshot (pre-crash); given the stock's subsequent ~90%+ decline from 2026 highs into the $0.60s, current market cap is materially lower than the $481M figure shown, but a current recalculation was not available from a dated source.
notes: SEC.gov, stocktitan.net, and benzinga.com full-article fetches failed in this session (network restrictions); figures are drawn from WebSearch summaries of those and other secondary outlets (RBR, finwire, barchart, panabee), not direct primary-document reads.
